questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, highlighters, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

The production possibility curve for an economy producing capital goods and consumer goods is represented by the line PQ. P capital goods T R O S Q consumer goods What is the opportunity cost of producing OS of consumer goods?

options.B: PR of capital goods
options.C: SQ of consumer goods
options.D: SQ of consumer goods + PR of capital goods

questions.questionText: How is labour allocated in a market economy and in a planned economy? market economy planned economy

options.A: according to changes in wage levels according to the profit motive
options.B: according to demand and according to input-output analysis supply in product markets
options.C: according to government decisions according to the price mechanism
options.D: according to government microeconomic according to consumer surplus and macroeconomic policies

questions.questionText: A person who has bought a DVD player using a credit card does not have to settle the account until 56 days after making the purchase. What function of money is illustrated by this delay in settlement?

options.A: medium of exchange
options.B: standard of deferred payment
options.C: store of value
options.D: unit of account

questions.questionText: When will the demand curve for motorcycles shift to the left?

options.A: when the price of cars falls
options.B: when the price of motorcycles falls
options.C: when the tax on motorcycles rises
options.D: when the price of public transport rises

options.A: high price elasticity of demand
options.B: low price elasticity of demand
options.C: totally inelastic price elasticity of demand
options.D: unitary price elasticity of demand

questions.questionText: Which government policy might limit the rationing function of the price mechanism?

options.A: the imposition of tariffs on imported consumer goods
options.B: the levy of indirect taxes at varying rates on different goods
options.C: the payment of subsidies to food producers
options.D: the setting of maximum prices for rented housing

questions.questionText: A government is planning to intervene in a market to fix output at the socially desirable level by giving a subsidy. MSC = MPC T costs/ Y benefits S X MSB MPB O R W output To achieve its objective, what should be the subsidy per unit?

options.A: ST B SX C TY D XY

questions.questionText: Which statement is correct?

options.A: External benefit minus private benefit equals social benefit.
options.B: Private benefit minus external benefit equals social benefit.
options.C: Social benefit minus external benefit equals private benefit.
options.D: Social benefit plus private benefit equals external benefit.

questions.questionText: A government carries out a cost-benefit analysis on the building of a new airport. It calculates that the cost of constructing and running the airport will be less than the revenue the airport will generate. It also estimates that benefits to third parties will be greater than the cost to third parties. Which reason might the government give for not building this airport?

options.A: The external costs exceed the external benefits.
options.B: The net private benefit is greater on another project.
options.C: The net social benefit is greater on another project.
options.D: The social costs exceed the social benefits.

questions.questionText: What is a defining characteristic of a public good?

options.A: An increase in consumption by one individual leaves the quantity available to others unchanged.
options.B: Consumption of the good by one individual confers benefits on other individuals.
options.C: The benefits obtained by those who consume the good are greater than they themselves realise.
options.D: The good is consumed jointly by all members of society.

questions.questionText: A government introduces a maximum price for house rentals (maxPh) and a minimum price for cleaning services (minPc). Both markets have identical demand and supply curves. Which diagram shows that the maximum price will be effective and the minimum price will be ineffective in the respective markets?

options.A: B S S maxPh minPc price price minPc maxPh
options.D: D O quantity O quantity
options.C: D S S maxPh minPc price price maxPh minPc

questions.questionText: The diagram represents the production possibility curves of two economies X and Y. X X agricultural goods (units) Y 0 500 1000 manufactured goods (units) As a result of soil erosion in economy X, the production possibility curve shifts from X to X . According to the law of comparative advantage, what should country Y do following this change?

options.A: cease to trade with country X
options.B: export agricultural goods to country X
options.C: export manufactured goods to country X
options.D: import both agricultural and manufactured goods from country X

questions.questionText: What is an assumption behind the basic theory of comparative advantage?

options.A: Each country sets its own tariff barriers.
options.B: Factors of production are mobile between countries.
options.C: Producers benefit from economies of scale.
options.D: There are no significant transport costs.

questions.questionText: Which statement about the impact of a quota and a tariff is correct?

options.A: A quota benefits the seller of the imports while a tariff raises government revenue.
options.B: A quota decreases the quantity of imports while a tariff leaves the quantity of imports unchanged.
options.C: A quota leaves import prices unchanged while a tariff raises the price of imports.
options.D: A quota shifts the demand curve for imports while a tariff shifts the supply curve of imports.

questions.questionText: At present, one unit of a country’s currency exchanges for US$1.2. The country aims to set its exchange rate at US$1.4. Which combination of government actions in the foreign exchange market must achieve this aim?

options.B: buying US currency and selling its own currency
options.C: selling US currency and buying its own currency
options.D: selling US currency and selling its own currency
